_README.title: SafeScroll Australia — Data File Maintenance Guide
_README.purpose: This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for all SafeScroll Australia statistics, platform risk scores, research findings, and reference data. The AI assistant reads this file directly via the Cloudflare Worker, and the website displays values from it. To update facts on both at once, edit only this file.
howToUpdate: 1. Click the pencil icon at the top right of this file on GitHub
2. Find the value you want to change using Ctrl+F
3. Edit the value, source, year, or url as needed
6. The AI assistant will reflect changes within 5 minutes (Worker cache TTL)
7. The website displays update at the same time
rulesForContributors: Only add data sourced from .gov.au, .edu.au, or academic research publications
Always include a working source URL — verify the link works before committing
Use exact values from the source — do not round, estimate, or infer
Do not delete entries unless data is genuinely incorrect — instead, update the value
If unsure whether to add something, open an Issue first to discuss
Keep statements neutral and factual — no editorial opinion in this file
validationChecklist: Source URL works and points to the cited publication
Source organisation is reputable (government, academic, or established research body)
Value matches what the source actually states
Metric description is precise — explains what the number measures
No defamatory or speculative claims about platforms

_README.ifYouNeedHelp: Open an Issue at https://github.com/ai-ati/safescroll-australia/issues with the label 'data-question'. Do not edit this file if you are unsure — incorrect data could mislead families and harm the project's credibility.

legislation.name: Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024
legislation.summary: World-first legislation requiring age-restricted social media platforms to take 'reasonable steps' to prevent Australians under 16 from creating or keeping an account. In eSafety's view this includes Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X, YouTube, Kick and Reddit.
legislation.limitations: Does not address algorithmic architecture; cannot prevent technical circumvention; logged-out viewing (e.g. YouTube without an account) remains possible; excluded services such as Discord and Roblox remain accessible

researchFindings.summary: Strongest evidence base of any social media harm category. Effects mediated by social comparison amplified by recommendation algorithms.
researchFindings.citation: Dane and Bhatia, PLOS Global Public Health 2023

researchFindings.summary: Social media disrupts sleep, which independently mediates mental health deterioration. Compounding harm pathway.
researchFindings.citation: Alonzo et al., Sleep Medicine Reviews 2021

researchFindings.summary: Mental wellbeing of Australians aged 15-24 declined since approximately 2012, coinciding with smartphone and social media adoption.
researchFindings.citation: Leigh et al., Australian Economic Review 2025

researchFindings.summary: Restricting age of access may reduce exposure but does not address the underlying algorithmic architecture that drives harm.
researchFindings.citation: Blake et al., Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry 2025

researchFindings.summary: Comprehensive parental and school-based education must accompany regulation to be effective.
researchFindings.citation: Champion et al., Child and Adolescent Mental Health 2025
